title: Streamlit Crashing with Error: `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

**UPDATE**: I believe the culprit is a bug in the `[USER].cache_resource` logic and/or the way streamlit handles db connections that try to persist (had same issues using `session_state`). See my follow-up message below. 

My initial issue:

Unfortunately I have a fairly complicated app. My streamlit application is crashing and I'm not sure why. The error seems somewhat ominous, but there's really not much information that helps me figure out what's going on, which is why I've made this issue. 

I've seen this error on rare occasion when building my complex application. Normally, this happens after I update the file and hit 'rerun', so I just chalk it up to: something happens when I hot-reload a new version of the file that breaks things. Nothing I'm concerned about since I don't expect to do this in production.

However, after adding a normal [selectbox](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/widgets/st.selectbox), streamlit intermittently crashes when I use [this](https://github.com/hoggatt/st-combobox) simple custom component that gives me the ability to define my own auto complete function. I don't actually think it's related to the combobox itself, it's just that when the combobox is auto-completing, it's rerunning a lot. This was working before I added a normal `st.textbox`, but now it's completely broken. However, the fact that I saw it very infrequently before indicates to me it's probably not directly related to the selectbox. 


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# THIS IS PSEUDO-CODE #

search_input = st.text_input()

...
many conditional statements doing something with the search input including setting st.experimental_set_query_params at one point
also queries the database using a cached_resource mysql connector (see below)
...

value = st.selectbox(items based on search_input)

# allow selecting something using a combobox (st-combobox) with autocomplete
def search_files(searchterm):
  refine search based (in part) on value
selected_value = st_combobox(search_files, ...)

# this method is cached
file = get_file(selected_value)

...
setting up controls for the plot based on the file loaded
uses st.experimental_set_query_params at some point
no database or complex cached stuff
...

# make plotly plot(s) here
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Unfortunately I'm not able to figure out exactly why this happens. It doesn't seem to happen consistently. 

However, often I see this error nearby: `2013 (HY000): Lost connection to MySQL server during query`. 

I have a method that looks like this:
```
[USER].cache_resource
def loaddb():
    creds = ...
    dbconn = SQL("EXAMPLE", "example.com", creds["username"], creds["password"], True)
    return dbconn
```

### Expected Behavior

I expect this crash not to happen. 

### Current Behavior

This is all that happens. Streamlit prints out two lines in the console, then hard-crashes:
```
free(): double free detected in tcache 2
Aborted
```

Sometimes I see this error too (maybe it's related to the cache_resource having issues?):
```
2013 (HY000): Lost connection to MySQL server during query
```
This error doesn't seem to crash outright, but something tells me it's related. 

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.26.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Ubuntu 20.04
- Browser: Brave Version 1.57.62, Chromium: 116.0.5845.180 (Official Build) (64-bit)


### Additional Information

I'm going to be trying to nail down exactly why this issue is happening over the next few days (try to figure out how to reproduce it) but I wanted to make the issue now since it seems like a very strange error someone on the team might have insight into.

comments_data.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-7336)

With some further digging, I've found out two very useful pieces of information:

1. If I type slowly into the combobox (so the app reloads less frequently), it does not crash nearly as often. 
2. If I remove the `@st.cache_resource` decorator from the `loaddb()` method described above, the app seems to work without any issues no matter how quickly/often it reloads (although the db connection is no longer cached). For those of you looking for a more satisfactory solution than "don't use cache", unfortunately the [st.session_state](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/session-state) api causes the same issues.

### My non-expert opinion

This `free(): double free detected in tcache 2` error is being generated in c++ or c code (possibly cpython stuff). My guess is that something in the `cache_resource` logic doesn't like very rapidly reloading the app (especially when the app has more complexity). My initial research indicates some variable is being freed in memory, then some other variable is being assigned to it. However, this only seems to happen in situations with more complex applications and frequent reloads. Since the `cache_resource` function is newer, my guess is there is some bug that shows up under these conditions with multiple threads/restarts. I hope this helps someone figure out what is going on.

I ran into the same error/behavior when trying to use `session_state` to store the database connection. This is strange and points to something a big deeper than just the cache_resource logic. Looks like restarting quickly in general + database connections that try to persist in any way cause issues.

I agree with your guess that it is coming from some C/C++ code, probably triggered by many reruns starting in separate threads at the same time and accessing the same database connection instance. Unfortunately this will be difficult to debug, and it isn't clear what we could do about it.
Closing this issue due to inactivity and it appears that it might not be directly related to Streamlit.

title: Preserve Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position in st.dataframe
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Today, when a page is refreshed / app gets rerun / data for dataframe changes, the dataframe completely refreshes. Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position are lost. 

This makes it hard to work with data within the dataframe and change it by means of a Master Detail View for example.

Idea is: Preserve Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position in st.dataframe when data is reloaded / the page is rerun.


### Why?

Scenario: A Master Detail View: The dataframe is part of the Master View within the page, and the Detail View enables the user to edit certain fields (not all are visible in the dataframe). After changing some data, the dataframe is reloaded and selection, sorting, scrolling position are lost.

### How?

The selection currently is set in the session, but it is not considered when the page is reloaded. 

Sorting is not part of the state.

Scrolling position is preserved for st.container today, but not for st.dataframe.

Solution idea:
- Store selection and sorting in session_state and use this information when the page is rerun and the dataframe is rendered.
- Use the implementation of st.container to preserve scrolling position.

### Additional Context


This issue is related to, however they only cover parts of this idea. 

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8851
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10128

body:

### Summary

In attempt to create a dynamic filter in a dialog box, I stumbled on the fact updating a session_state variable via a custom component is not possible. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
Something as simple as this code does not execute:

    st.session_state["test_text"] = None 

[USER].experimental_dialog(title="Test", width="small")
def test_dialog():

    import streamlit_antd_components as sac

    def onChangeTest():

        st.session_state["test_text"] = st.session_state["testing123"] 
    

    sac.chip(
        items=[
            sac.ChipItem(label='apple'),
            sac.ChipItem(label='google'),
            sac.ChipItem(label='github', icon='github'),
            sac.ChipItem(label='twitter', icon='twitter'),

    )
    st.write(st.session_state["test_text"])

st.button("Test", key="test_btn")

```

But it works with native widgets:

st.button("Test", key="test_btn")

```
```

_No response_

Just like the native code updates in the dialog, I expect custom components to also update in the dialog. But it only works for native widgets and not the custom components.

title: st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.slider` accepts `date`/`datetime` bounds that the frontend cannot represent exactly, and silently snaps them to a different instant instead of reporting the problem. The `int` and `float` paths already validate and raise a helpful `StreamlitAPIException`; the timelike path does not.

Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and held in a JavaScript number on the frontend, so only about **1684-07-28 to 2255-06-05** round-trips exactly. Outside that, precision is lost.

`lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py` acknowledges the gap:

```python
elif all_timelikes:
    # No validation yet. TODO: check between 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31
    pass
```

Worth noting the TODO's own target range is wrong — most of `0001`–`9999` is not representable, so validating to those limits would not have fixed it.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import datetime as dt
import streamlit as st

# Silently accepted, but min_value cannot be represented exactly:
st.slider("historical", min_value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(1700, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1))

# Also silently accepted, both bounds unrepresentable:
st.slider("projection", min_value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(2400, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1))

# Raises a bare OverflowError instead of a StreamlitAPIException:
st.slider("ancient", value=dt.date(1, 1, 1))
```

### Actual Behavior

Inspecting the serialized proto shows the bounds exceeding JavaScript's `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with no error raised:

```
in-range 1900..2000      -> NO ERROR. min=-2208988800000000 max=946684800000000  JS-unsafe: none
historical 1600..1700    -> NO ERROR. min=-11676096000000000                      JS-unsafe: ['min']
far future 2300..2400    -> NO ERROR. min=10413792000000000 max=13569465600000000 JS-unsafe: ['min', 'max']
min date 0001..0002      -> OverflowError: date value out of range
```

Two distinct problems:

1. **Moderately out-of-range values are accepted and lose precision.** Years like 1600 or 2300 are ordinary in historical datasets and long-range projections, so this is not just an exotic edge case.
2. **Extreme values raise a bare `OverflowError`.** It comes from `prepared_value[0] - timedelta(days=14)`, which computes the *default* `min_value`/`max_value` even when the caller supplied both explicitly, and overflows next to `date.min`/`date.max`. This is not a `StreamlitAPIException`, so it surfaces as an unhandled Python error rather than actionable guidance.

### Expected Behavior

Out-of-range timelike bounds should raise a `StreamlitAPIException` naming the representable range, matching how the int and float paths already behave. Extreme values should produce that same message rather than an `OverflowError`.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (reproduced at `f2648d7237`)
- Python version: 3.14.5
- OS: macOS 15.5

### Additional Information

Contrast with the existing int path, which is what the timelike path should mirror:

```
`max_value` (9007199254740992) must be <= (1 << 53) - 1
```

comments_data.body:
This is a valid bug in `st.slider`'s date/datetime path. Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and sent as JavaScript numbers, which only preserve exact integers within `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (~±2^53, roughly 1684–2255). Int/float sliders already reject out-of-range bounds via `JSNumber.validate_*_bounds`, but the timelike branch is explicitly a no-op (`# No validation yet`), so moderately out-of-range dates are accepted and silently lose precision. Separately, default `min_value`/`max_value` are always computed as `value ± timedelta(days=14)` before checking whether the caller supplied bounds, which raises a bare `OverflowError` near `date.min`/`date.max` instead of a `StreamlitAPIException`. Fixing this should validate the microsecond form against JS safe-integer limits (not the incorrect 0001–9999 TODO range) and avoid computing unused default bounds that can overflow.

### Related Issues

- [#7427](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7427) — `st.date_input` overflows when computing default selectable bounds near `datetime.max` (similar “default range buffer overflows date extrema” pattern; different widget).
- [#5099](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5099) — `st.slider` bounds-validation inconsistency vs `st.number_input` when `value` is outside `min`/`max` (related to slider bound checking, but not about JS safe-integer / date precision).

No duplicate found for silent JS-precision loss on date/datetime `st.slider` values.

title: Add a button group widget with trigger (click) mode
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Provide a button group that supports **trigger (click) mode** instead of selection mode — i.e. a horizontal group of buttons that returns the clicked value once (like `st.button`) and clears after the rerun, rather than persisting a selection. This can either be a new `st.button_group` command or an extension of the existing `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`.

### Why?

It's currently a bit complicated to build things like quick selections / quick replies for chat UIs (a major need for LLM-powered apps), button toolbars, dialog action rows (Confirm / Cancel / Clear), or clickable example grids. Today you have to combine many individual `st.button`s across `st.columns`, which is a lot of boilerplate and looks messy because wrapping depends on each button's label length.

### How?

Two main options:

**Option 1 — Extend `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` with a trigger mode:**

```python
st.pills(..., selection_mode="single" | "multi" | "trigger")
```

In `trigger` mode the widget doesn't keep state: it returns the clicked value and clears it after the rerun (like a button), returning `None` otherwise. `default` wouldn't be allowed in this mode.

**Option 2 — Add a dedicated `st.button_group` command (preferred):**

```python
st.button_group(
    options,
    *,
    format_func=None,
    key=None,
    on_click=None,
    args=None,
    kwargs=None,
    disabled=False,
    type="default" | "rounded",
    wrap=True,
)
```

Behaves like `st.pills` but tailored for triggers: no top label/help (not needed for quick selections), `on_click` instead of `on_change` (aligns with `st.button`), a `type` option for a rounded pill-like look, and a `wrap` option. Keeping triggers in a separate command avoids overloading the selection API (e.g. `selection_mode="trigger"` reads oddly, `default` becomes incompatible, and typing gets awkward).

### Additional Context

- Related: #8318 (quick replies/suggestions for chat responses) — one of the primary motivating use cases.
- Other use cases: button toolbars, dialog action rows, and clickable example grids.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16375)

This is an enhancement request for a **trigger-mode button group**: a horizontal set of options that behaves like `st.button` (returns the clicked value once, then clears) rather than like `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` (persistent selection). The preferred shape is a dedicated `st.button_group` API; an alternative is extending `selection_mode` with `"trigger"`. Today, workarounds require many `st.button`s in `st.columns`, which is boilerplate-heavy and wraps poorly. Internally, `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` already share `button_group.py` with only `single`/`multi` click modes, so this would either add a third click mode or a thin trigger-oriented public command on that shared implementation.

### Related Issues

- [#8318 – Quick replies/suggestions for chat user response](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8318): Explicitly cited in the issue; a primary motivating use case (suggestion chips / quick replies) that a trigger-mode button group would enable.
- [#10740 – Add a configurable toolbar or clickable actions to `st.chat_message`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10740): Related chat UI need for clickable action rows; a trigger button group could be a building block for message-level actions.
- [#16240 – Add a stateful button](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16240): Complementary button-semantics proposal (persistent toggle-styled button vs. this issue’s ephemeral click group); not a duplicate, but adjacent API design.

title: Add a `type="cards"` variant to `st.radio` for a card/bordered design
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.radio` with a `"cards"` variant that renders each option as a bordered, selectable card (with the selected card highlighted) instead of the default radio-button list. Same widget behavior — only the visual style changes. See [Tremor's Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group) for the look.

### Why?

Card-style single-select is a very common, more prominent and touch-friendly pattern for choosing between a few richer options (e.g. plans, payment methods, layouts, modes). Today users approximate it with columns + bordered containers + buttons/`st.radio` and a lot of manual state/CSS work. A built-in `"cards"` variant makes this polished pattern a one-liner.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
choice = st.radio(
    "Choose a plan",
    ["Starter", "Pro", "Enterprise"],
    captions=[
        "For individuals getting started",
        "For growing teams",
        "Advanced controls & support",
    ],
    type="cards",
)
```

- `type="default"` — current radio-button list.
- `type="cards"` — render each option as a bordered card; the selected option is visually highlighted.
- Keep existing params working (`captions`, `horizontal`, `format_func`, `index=None`, etc.). Captions map naturally to a description line inside each card.

**Alternative solution — a `border: bool` parameter:** Instead of a `type` enum, just add `st.radio(..., border=True)` that wraps each option in a bordered card. This mirrors the `border` parameter on `st.container` and keeps the API minimal. Downside: it's less extensible than a `type` enum if we later want more visual variants (e.g. `"pills"`), and it's a boolean rather than a named style.

### Additional Context

- Reference designs:
  - [Tremor — Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group)
  - [Tailwind Plus — Radio Groups (card designs)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/forms/radio-groups)
  - [streamlit-extras — Card Selector](https://extras.streamlit.app/?extra=%F0%9F%83%8F+Card+Selector) (existing community implementation)
- Related: #2325 (`st.radio` with sections), #7184 (stretch horizontal radio), #11959 (consistent API for selectbox/pills/segmented_control/radio).

Enhancement request to add an optional `type` parameter to `st.radio` (`"default"` | `"cards"`) so options can render as bordered, selectable cards (Tremor-style radio card group) while keeping existing radio semantics and params (`captions`, `horizontal`, `format_func`, etc.). title: File_uploader() - ValueError: I/O operation on closed file.

comments_data.body: I have the similar requirement and I am facing the same issue as mentioned above. Is there a workaround?
Closing as a duplicate #2235. Also resolved in #2279
It looks like this is still happening intermittently in v0.71.0. Reopening

From Thiago:
> My 100% blind guess is we're creating a single file-like-object on upload and reusing it on every run — so if the file is closed and then gets reused it will brerak. To fix, we'd create a new file-like object each time.

Instead, when running on the main page and not on the sidebar, everythng works fine:
```

    input_file = st.file_uploader(
        "Input your file", type=[".csv"]

```

comments_data.body:
Hi @ElenaBossolini ! Thanks for the report. I see how this does not work, and it may benefit from some more clarity. We should probably show some warning when in a `with` syntax as that determines the location of an element when you use `st`.

Will tag `docs` on this just so they are aware this might benefit from clarity in the docs.

Hi @kmcgrady , thank you for taking a look at the issue.
As I understand from your reply, it is fine by you that we cannot have a `file_uploader` within a `beta_expander` in the `sidebar`. But that is a functionality that in my opinion it would be really nice to have! 
I usually use the `sidebar` as the input area, while in the main page I show the results of the simulation.
While my application grows bigger, also the number of inputs grows, and my users are keen in keeping an easy-to-read input sidebar. The `beta_expander` would be such a good way to do that, so that one can collapse all `file_uploaders` within it!

Hey @ElenaBossolini,

What @kmcgrady means with:

> We should probably show some warning when in a with syntax as that determines the location of an element when you use st.

is when you write the following:

```python
with st.sidebar.beta_expander("Input file", expanded=True):
    xxx
```

any `st` call at the **xxx** level will place Streamlit elements inside the sidebar beta_expander, because you're in the `with st.sidebar.beta_expander` with block.

So when you write:

```python
with st.sidebar.beta_expander("Input file", expanded=True):
    input_file = st.sidebar.file_uploader(
        "Input your file", type=[".csv"]
    )
```

you're trying to define a sidebar inside the sidebar beta_expander, which results in a nested sidebar (which is not possible in Streamlit), and then put a file_uploader in this nested sidebar which does not exist, so it seems to just appear from nowhere.

Hence the correct syntax is:

```python
with st.sidebar.beta_expander("Input file", expanded=True):
    input_file = st.file_uploader(
        "Input your file", type=[".csv"]
    )
```

We will try to document this behavior better, context managers is a powerful feature that may not be as understood as other Python native features :) 

Have a nice day,
Fanilo

comments_data.body: I have the same issue. Never thought it is due to unique method. I can track from the logs it is triggered again and already discussed in forum, but can't find the problem.

@PierXuY Thanks for reporting this issue. I was able to reproduce this [here](https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-6182). I believe that this is the same root issue as https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6236.

Hey @PierXuY @koftezz @benjamin-breton-loreal 👋 

Good news! In the next Streamlit release (1.24.0), we're bringing back `hash_funcs` but to the new caching primitives 😄 (added by #6502).

That allows you to override Streamlit's hashing of `numpy.ndarray` based on its id (note: df.unique() returns a numpy array). Here's an example you can use to verify it works.. available in `streamlit-nightly==1.23.2.dev20230614`:

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

@st.cache_data
def get_data():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"num":[112,112,2,3],"str":['be','a','be','c']})
    return df

@st.cache_data(hash_funcs={np.ndarray: str})
def show_data(data):
    time.sleep(1)
    return data

df = get_data()
data = df['str'].unique()

index_daily_data = show_data(data)
st.dataframe(index_daily_data)
st.button("rerun")
```

Notice how `show_data` is **_not called_** repeatedly 👇 

![hash_numpy](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/20672874/8abe74c6-c365-4d77-aaf4-a5bfdb990415)

Hey hey @PierXuY @koftezz @benjamin-breton-loreal, @LukasMasuch  my 2 cents here

After some investigation I found that problem you facing here happens because of pandas `Series.unique()` in conjuction with python string data type returns numpy array with dtype="object" . 

And the memory buffer for the corresponding array is different on each subsequent rerun. So numpy_array.tobytes() returns new bytes that could not be cached deterministically (we use .tobytes() for internal hashing here). 

This happens only when type of corresponding column is "object", and works correctly for primitive types. 
So if you cast your unique result to string dtype, it would work as expected:

```python
...
df = get_data()

data = df['str'].unique()
data = data.astype("str")

index_daily_data = show_data(data)
...
```

Hey @PierXuY 

After discussing this internally, we decided to close this issue. The problem is with the `unique` method when it applies to the Python str type. 

The solutions described in the comments should work!

comments_data.body: @binste Thanks a lot for reporting this before the actual release! I created a quick fix to pin the major Altair version to `<5` and we will start investigating supporting/upgrading to Altair version 5. I believe our frontend is anyways already using vega 5 and the breaking changes don't look too problematic.
@binste Do you know when Altair 5 is planned to be released?

Great, thank you for looking into it! There is no fixed release date yet but it's likely going to be a few weeks. There are some limitations with the current Altair 5 release candidate which are documented [here](https://github.com/altair-viz/altair/issues/2937#issue-1605677103). They require changes in Vega-Lite which are ongoing. Once there is a new VL version (likely to be 5.7) the Altair 5 release will be built against it. Not sure how you pinned VL in your frontend but it might make sense to then upgrade Streamlit as well to use the newest VL version.

Feel free to ping me if you have any questions on the changes or on the depedency on the VL release!

@binste Thanks for the update 👍 I started a draft PR https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/6618. I haven't looked too much into it yet, but it seems that the Altair tests are consistently failing with:

```
>       self.assertEqual(chart_spec["mark"], "line")
E       AssertionError: {'type': 'line'} != 'line'
```
for example in this line: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/cec1c141f7858e31f8200a9cdc42b8ddd09ab0e7/lib/tests/streamlit/elements/arrow_altair_test.py#L145

This is probably something that has changed in the chart spec, or?

Exactly. Prior to version 5, if a mark did not have any additional options (`alt.Chart().mark_line()`) Altair used the shorthand mark spec: `"mark": "line"`. Once a mark option was added (`alt.Chart().mark_line(color="blue")`), the spec got expanded into `"mark": {"type": "line", "color": "blue"}`. This was changed in https://github.com/altair-viz/altair/pull/2823 so that the expanded mark spec is always used. You can find the reasoning in that PR but in short it was about making it easier to write these kind of tests that you have, e.g. for autograding of student assignments.

-> You can now always access the type of the mark with `chart_spec["mark"]["type"]`.

Altair RC3 is out. Changes compared to RC2 are that it's built against [VL 5.8](https://github.com/vega/vega-lite/releases/tag/v5.8.0) which just came out and that we set a minimum required jsonschema version of `>=4.0.1`. Previously it was `>=3`.

@binste Thanks :) that makes sense! One more question: which import would you recommend us within Streamlit:

1. `from altair.vegalite.v5.api import Chart`
2. `from altair.vegalite.api import Chart`
3. `from altair import Chart`

I have updated everything to `from altair.vegalite.api import Chart` in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/6618, but I'm wondering if `from altair import Chart` is the more stable/official import?
I agree, from altair import chart is very unlikely to be changed and the best option for streamlit. :)

title: Widget display value depends on ScriptRunner completing execution of a different page (or not)
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using `st.session_state` to pre-set the value of a widget, the widget will sometimes appear to have a blank/0 value that does not match the value returned by the DeltaGenerator function call, and this behavior depends on the user switching from a different Streamlit "page" which did or did not finish running to completion.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# Create a multipage streamlit app

# -- in testpage1.py
import streamlit as st

st.write("Starting")
st.session_state.setdefault("my_widget", "Hello World")
text_value = st.text_input("Enter some text", key="my_widget")
st.write(text_value)
st.button("press to refresh")

# -- in testpage2.py
import streamlit as st
from time import sleep

st.write("starting")
sleep(10)
st.write("finished")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start streamlit with a fresh session on testpage1.py
2. See: "Hello World" in the `my_widget` text_input and "Hello World" printed below it via `st.write`
3. Change the text of the `my_widget` text_input to something else. This step is not strictly required to reproduce the bug but allows you to verify that A) the `.setdefault` call is working as expected and B) that the value has "reset" to the default "Hello World" later on.
4. Navigate to testpage2. Allow 10 seconds for the script to run to completion, so that "Finished" is displayed
5. Navigate back to testpage1.
6. See: "Hello World" in the `my_widget` text_input and "Hello World" printed below it via `st.write`. The input and display state of the widget has been reset to it's default value, and this makes sense, since widgets do not retain their state across page changes.
7. Navigate to testpage2. Before the 10 seconds has elapsed, navigate back to testpage1.
8. See "" (blank) in the `my_widget` text_input, and "Hello World" printed below it via `st.write`. This is unexpected, as the widget visual state does not match the returned value nor the pre-set value that it should have because of the `st.session_state.setdefault` call right before it.
9. Clicking the "press to refresh" button causes the "Hello World" written by `st.write` to disappear (due to the fact that the front-end sends the blank widget state to the backend as part of the ReRun Data for the button press)

### Expected Behavior

Widget visual state on testpage1 reload does not depend on when testpage2 execution was interrupted.

### Current Behavior

Widget visual state on testpage1 reload DOES seem to depend on when testpage2 execution was interrupted.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.26.0
- Python version: 3.11.4
- Operating System: Centos Stream 9 and Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome v116, opera v101.0.4843.43


### Additional Information

This issue may be related to https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6146 and/or https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6074, but I believe it is distinct (or at least a distinct manifestation of an underlying issue that has not been completely resolved) due to the behavior dependence on the lack of completion of a prior ScriptRunner.

This behavior doesn't seem to appear with the option off + the sleep doesn't disable buttons and navigation with the option on, so I'm guessing this is the case.

I do think this may be related to some work we're looking into in #7373, though (CC @AnOctopus)

This is an unfortunate consequence of how we handle the transience of widget state, and can't be fixed until we address widget persistence.

Streamlit used to work by always doing cleanup of "stale widgets" after a script run finished, even if it finished because it was interrupted. This would usually not be noticed because a rerun request would include the state of the widgets in the web app, even if they were just around because the active script run hadn't gotten to them yet. For fast reruns, we changed it so that interrupted runs wouldn't do the cleanup, though I can't recall exactly our reasoning for it and couldn't readily find it. We later made fast reruns the default.

That is the story for a single page app. For MPA, both [widgets on other pages persist] and [widgets on other pages reset] are perfect for some apps but would break others, and addressing it will be a big project, so we haven't done it yet. In the meantime, we get this awkward middle ground, where the persistence of widget state on another page depends on if the current page finished running before you switch back. We could try to fix it, but that would break other apps. A proper fix will require a notion of widget persistence.

In the meantime, as @vdonato notes, this behavior can be worked around by turning off fast reruns, though that will generally reduce responsiveness of script reruns.

@AnOctopus Thanks for the run through --  it in line with my own understanding of how widgets and state interact with the "fast" reruns.  Like you said, you can't really call the current behavior of widget state in the python application a "bug" vs a "feature".

I do, however, want to re-focus on this particular line from the recreation steps:

> See "" (blank) in the my_widget text_input, and "Hello World" printed below it via st.write. 

_After_ the fast re-run happens, it seems like there is a disconnect between the _python value of a widget_ and the _frontend value of a widget_. This seems like a "true" bug; if the widget state has persisted thru the page change (as indicated by the "Hello World" printed via `st.write`) then should not also the front end component that renders the `text_input` UI element receive a protobuf with that "Hello World" state in it and render it to the DOM with the text filled out? That's how it works in most other cases when a fast page change _doesn't_ happen.

In my estimation this particular aspect seems more like a front-end / back-end communication issue, but I will admit I do not know how the front-end receives, queues, and handles protobuf messages on page changes.

In other words, _any_ of the following outcomes would be consistent with your explanation above, but _none_ of them is what's actually happening.

> Set the text_input widget value to "Hello Octopus" on testpage1.
> Navigate to testpage2. Before the 10 seconds has elapsed, navigate back to testpage1.

1. **Outcome 1:** See "" (blank) in the my_widget text_input, and "" (blank) printed below it via st.write. This indicates that the widget state has been somehow been "lost" but that the front-end is in control of the (now blank) value.
2. **Outcome 2:** See "Hello World" in the my_widget text_input, and "Hello World" printed below it via st.write. This indicates that the widget state has been reset and the back-end is in control of the value.
3. **Outcome 3:** See "Hello Octopus" in the my_widget text_input, and "Hello Octopus" printed below it via st.write. This indicates that the widget state has been persisted, and the back-end is in control of the value.

Some thoughts that I thought would paint a more complete picture but ended up not actually leading me anywhere...

1. Text_input widgets only forward a new value to the front-end as part of the proto when the value has been detected to have changed (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/text_widgets.py#L332)
2. This value_changed flag is set when the widget is registered, and depends on whether the user_key for the widget is already present in _new_session_state or not (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py#L621). 
4. This would appear to possibly relate to the whole "session state preservation thing", but I can't quite piece together why there is a difference in behavior between waiting for testpage2 to run to completion or not.

Is there an easy way to turn on debug Protobuffer logging either on the Python or JS side to see what's getting sent over?

EDIT:
* Is it possible the Runtime _thinks_ that the client has a FwdMessage cached on it's side when in actuality the Client does not? The Runtime seems to only remove expired entries when a SCRIPT_FINISHED message is received, which might be what's not happening when testpage2 doesn't run to completion. (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/runtime/runtime.py#L692)

There is no builtin way to turn on outgoing protobuf logging, but adding a print line in `ScriptRunner._enqueue_forward_msg` is easy and effective.

I don't think the forward message cache will be relevant here, IIRC it only gets used for messages over some size threshold.

I have some vague ideas about possible causes and am debugging this now.

My trace of what is happening:
1. the script runs, putting "Hello World" in the new session state
2. this is seen as new information, so it is sent as part of the protobuf for the text_input, and is used as the initial value
3. We put a new value in the text_input, which saves it in the `WidgetStateManager` and sends the rerun request with that value
4. We click the radio to change pages, sending a rerun request for that page
5. this rerun triggers a new session, and since the page has changed, `clearAppState` is called, which removes the value from WidgetStateManager
6. as setup for the rerun, the widget value for the text input is moved to old session state
7. we click the radio to go back to the first page
8. the text input is registered in the script rerun, where it gets the value from old session state, but it does not put that value in the protobuf, because it is not new (and assumes the frontend would have it)
9. the text input is rendered, but it has no value in the WidgetStateManager, and we did not set a default value, so it initializes with a `null` value, which renders as blank

Based on this, changing the frontend reset somehow is probably the right kind of fix, but it would need to be done cautiously, to avoid other situations keeping around state they shouldn't.

@AnOctopus Did you or the team figure out yet what the long-term behavior of SessionState should be around page changes? 

I did some testing/logging of this too, I believe the behavior you describe is correct. 
When the user clicks on a page-change link, the frontend sends the re-run request to the backend and immediately clears its WidgetStateManager of inactive widgets (e.g. all of them, because the page is changing). However, the backend does not clear out old widget states until the active script_runner hits a "script finished" point. When this doesn't happen (because the user changed pages mid-run and fast-reruns are enabled), the old widget states are not removed.

There are two "root" issues going on:

### Issue 1: value-retention for widgets with user keys depends on previous script-runner finishing while active. 
This one is pretty easy to fix; but requires a choice.

> A. If the desire is to have user_key'd widgets retain their value across page changes the same way that custom user entries in `session_state` do, then the logic which cleans up widget states at the end of a script run needs to preserve those widgets' values -- it does not do so at present.

> B. If the desire is to have user_key'd widgets not retain their value across page changes, like widgets without a user_key, then ALL widget state needs to be cleared as soon as a re-run with a different page hash than the current one is requested.

### Issue 2: The desynchronization of WidgetStateManager (frontend) and SessionState (backend) when a page change occurs.
This is easy if you go with option B and commit to clearing ALL backend widget state every time a page changes. Nothing needs to get changed on the frontend because it's _already_ clearing it's widget state as soon as the page changes.

If you go with option A, then this is a lot tricker. Either, as you said above, the backend needs to send all the widget states it knows about to the front-end at the start of a re-run, OR the frontend WidgetStateManager needs to keep track of which widgets have a user_key, and purposefully avoid clearing those widgets' state when a page change is requested.

@Asaurus1 We haven't revisited the behavior of session state and page changes, no. The persistence of widgets is a very tricky design area with many competing use cases and we haven't wanted to open Pandora's box yet.

For issue 1, option B is the current intent, and I think you're right that we should fully clear the state of widgets from other pages. I will look into fixing this soon.
Just merged a fix, will be in the next release.

title: st.logo image blinks on each new page navigation
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Please make the image in st.logo not blink when navigating to new pages from the sidebar.

### Why?

I understand that the call to st.logo() is being run separately on each page of my multipage app, but is there some way to make the image not blink when I navigate to a new page from the sidebar? The sidebar itself (with all its page links) does not blink, so it seems possible despite the new call on each page. It's quite noticeable and can be disturbing/unexpected for many users.

### How?

Out of my scope of expertise, it's just a UI thing.

### Additional Context

_No response_
